column1: # Held-out stub corpus for the substring fallback and the tree path.
# Written after the AST detector and before the fallback was extended to read
# macros and thrown errors with arguments, and labelled by a rule fixed in
# advance of running either path on it (the same discipline as
# secrets_holdout*.tsv): a row is `stub` when its line, read as code, is a
# placeholder body whose only effect is to signal that the work is not done
# (a todo!/unimplemented! macro, a panic or thrown error whose message says
# not implemented / todo / implement me, Kotlin's TODO, Ruby's or Python's
# UnimplementedError, Swift's fatalError("not implemented")). It is `clean`
# when the same text is quoted, commented, an identifier, prose, or a real
# error that merely resembles one. Comment markers (a bare TODO note) are not
# part of this rule: they are advisory and measured elsewhere.
# It is deliberately not tuned to pass. Languages the fallback does not read
# (Swift, Scala, Dart, C) are in it on purpose: a recall figure that excluded
# them would describe the cases the gate was written for.
# Columns, TAB-separated: label (stub|clean), path, note, content.
# Measured by tests/stub_holdout.rs; the counts are quoted in rust/STATUS.md.
